landscape.label: 2026 Price Guide
title: Roof Replacement
Pricing Guide
landscape.say: How much does a new roof cost in Iowa City in 2026? Here's the pricing guide: the price ranges, what each type of roof costs, how Iowa weather affects your roof and your budget, and the extra costs to plan for.

landscape.label: 2026 Price Ranges
landscape.title: What a new roof costs in Iowa City
landscape.speak: Statewide, the average Iowa roof replacement costs about six thousand one hundred sixty dollars, with most homeowners spending four thousand seven hundred ninety-four dollars to fifteen thousand seven hundred seventy-nine dollars. In the Iowa City area, a full residential replacement typically runs about seven thousand eight hundred forty dollars to nineteen thousand six hundred dollars. And most standard-sized homes land between nine thousand eight hundred dollars and fourteen thousand seven hundred dollars.
landscape.say: Statewide, the average Iowa roof replacement costs about $6,160, with most homeowners spending $4,794 to $15,779. In the Iowa City area, a full residential replacement typically runs about $7,840 to $19,600. And most standard-sized homes land between $9,800 and $14,700.

landscape.label: Cost by Home Size
landscape.title: Iowa roof cost by home size
landscape.speak: Your home's size sets the baseline. In Iowa, a one-story, one thousand square foot home averages about seven thousand two hundred twenty-six dollars for a new roof. A fifteen hundred square foot home, about eight thousand seven hundred fifty-five dollars. A two-story, two thousand square foot home, about eight thousand nine hundred twenty-seven dollars. And a three thousand square foot home, about eleven thousand four hundred ninety-six dollars. The median Iowa home is just sixteen hundred twenty-three square feet.
landscape.say: Your home's size sets the baseline. In Iowa, a one-story, 1,000 square foot home averages about $7,226 for a new roof. A 1,500 square foot home, about $8,755. A two-story, 2,000 square foot home, about $8,927. And a 3,000 square foot home, about $11,496. The median Iowa home is just 1,623 square feet.

landscape.label: Cost by Roof Type
landscape.title: Iowa roof cost by type
landscape.speak: The type of roof you choose matters most. On a median-sized Iowa home, asphalt shingles cost about four thousand seven hundred ninety-four dollars, at four dollars sixty-five cents a square foot. Metal runs about eight thousand nine hundred eleven dollars. Wood shingles and shakes, about eleven thousand four hundred one dollars. Clay tile, about fifteen thousand seven hundred three dollars. And slate, the most expensive, about fifteen thousand seven hundred seventy-nine dollars, at fifteen dollars thirty cents a square foot.
landscape.say: The type of roof you choose matters most. On a median-sized Iowa home, asphalt shingles cost about $4,794, at $4.65 a square foot. Metal runs about $8,911. Wood shingles and shakes, about $11,401. Clay tile, about $15,703. And slate, the most expensive, about $15,779, at $15.30 a square foot.

landscape.speak: Which type fits Iowa? Asphalt shingles are the most popular and most affordable, and last about twenty to twenty-five years. Class four impact-resistant shingles are rated for hail up to two inches. Metal handles hail, wind, and heavy snow, and can last forty years or more. Wood looks classic, but Iowa's humid summers can cause rot and mold. Clay and slate last a long time, but they're heavy, need a specialist, and cost the most.

landscape.label: Iowa Weather Factors
landscape.title: How Iowa weather hits your roof

cards.name: Spring hail
cards.desc: Cracks shingles. Class 4 shingles can lower insurance premiums

cards.name: Straight-line winds
cards.desc: Lift shingles. Metal & wind-rated shingles hold on

cards.name: Ice dams
cards.desc: Back water under the eaves. Ice-and-water shield stops it

cards.name: Heavy snow
cards.desc: Adds weight. Metal sheds snow & handles the load

cards.name: Freeze-thaw cycles
cards.desc: Damage roof decking, which can add repair costs

cards.name: Humid summers
cards.desc: Promote rot & mold. Good ventilation is a must

landscape.speak: Iowa weather is a big part of the story. Spring hail cracks shingles, and class four shingles can even lower your insurance premiums. Straight-line winds in summer lift shingles, so metal and wind-rated shingles hold on better. Ice dams in winter back water up under the eaves, which is why you want ice-and-water shield along the eaves and valleys. Heavy snow adds weight, and metal sheds it. Freeze-thaw cycles damage roof decking, which can add repair costs. And humid summers promote rot and mold, so good ventilation is a must.

landscape.label: Storm Damage & Insurance
landscape.name: Storm damage replacement
landscape.desc: Often covered by homeowners insurance, minus your deductible.

bullets.t: Get the damage documented with photos
Have your roofer meet the adjuster on-site
Ask about Class 4 shingles for a premium discount

landscape.speak: If hail or wind took out your roof, homeowners insurance often covers the replacement, minus your deductible. Get the damage documented with photos, have your roofer meet the adjuster on-site, and ask about class four shingles, which can qualify for an insurance premium discount.

landscape.label: Other Costs
landscape.title: Other costs to plan for

cards.name: Tear-off
cards.desc: About 1.5 hours of labor per 100 sq ft of old roof

cards.name: Permits
cards.desc: Most Iowa cities require one for a full replacement

cards.name: Rotted decking
cards.desc: Bad wood found under the old roof gets replaced

cards.name: Hidden damage
cards.desc: 14% of homeowners paid more than their estimate

landscape.speak: Plan for a few extra costs. Tear-off takes about an hour and a half of labor per hundred square feet of old roof. Most Iowa cities require a permit for a full replacement. Rotted decking found under the old roof gets replaced. And hidden damage is the big one: about fourteen percent of homeowners said their final bill came in higher than their estimate.

landscape.label: Timing & Lifespan
landscape.title: When to replace, and how long it lasts
landscape.speak: The best time to replace a roof in Iowa is May through September, before snow and ice. The average Iowa roof lasts twenty to thirty years, while metal and tile can last forty or more. And good news: Iowa roofing prices run about one to two percent cheaper than Illinois and Wisconsin, and about twelve percent cheaper than Minnesota.
